title: Akamai current decision desk
status: Material demand signal · execution economics unresolved
purpose: Akamai's expanded Anthropic relationship materially strengthens the evidence for cloud-infrastructure demand. Management has supplied an expected ramp, but the deal does not yet establish recognized revenue, gross margin, cash return, realized dilution, or an expectation gap.

currentDecision.label: Decision today
currentDecision.detail: Treat the announced ramp as a management plan, not a reason to change the scenario model or make an investment conclusion. The next decision turns on deployment, revenue conversion, capacity economics, and the warrant's effect.

facts.label: Contracted commitment
facts.detail: Akamai disclosed a contractual Anthropic commitment, with potential for about $9B more. Contract value is not recognized revenue.

facts.label: FY2026 revenue guide
facts.detail: Akamai said the agreement does not change its FY2026 revenue guidance.

facts.label: Management ramp plan
facts.detail: Akamai's presentation expects service initiation in late Q2 2027, $150M–$300M of FY2027 delivery, and full contract run-rate by end-2028. These are management estimates, not recognized revenue.

facts.label: Capacity burden
facts.detail: Akamai estimates about $1.7B of incremental 2026 capital investment to secure and pre-purchase memory and related components.

facts.label: Conditional warrant
facts.value: 40% first tranche · up to 7.74M common-equivalent shares
facts.detail: The first 40% of warrant shares vests only on the first Project Plan 3 payment, subject to conditions; each later 20% tranche requires an additional $3B commitment. This is not already vested dilution.

nextQuestions.title: Does the announced ramp hold?
nextQuestions.detail: Test the late-Q2 2027 service plan against deployment milestones, revenue-recognition, remaining-performance-obligation or backlog disclosure, and the first reported contribution.

nextQuestions.title: What are the unit economics?
nextQuestions.detail: Look for price, gross-margin, cost-to-serve, capacity utilization, and duration information—not just another contract headline.

nextQuestions.title: Can Akamai fund it well?
nextQuestions.detail: Test capex, operating cash flow, free-cash-flow conversion, financing needs, and margin guidance against the added capacity burden.

nextQuestions.title: What is the concentration and warrant cost?
nextQuestions.detail: Clarify customer concentration, service and supply-chain dependencies, warrant accounting and vesting, and any actual share-count effect.

boundary: A signed commitment proves a customer and creates an obligation. It does not by itself prove recognized revenue, attractive gross margin, cash returns, realized dilution, or that market expectations are too low.
sourceNote: The conditional commitment, service/termination rights, supplier arrangements, and warrant triggers come from Akamai's September 24 Form 8-K; the capex and delivery plan come from the company presentation. The complete services and supplier agreements are expected as September-quarter 10-Q exhibits. These plans are not recognized revenue or reported project economics.
